note: Per-rule test-of-record. Covers every rule check_source runs from a single source string with no declaration and no project context. Parse gate: HC-SYN. Construction (section 4.1): HC003/HC006/HC007/HC011, HC-SM01/HC-SM02/HC-SM05. Single-file static purity (section 4.2): HC-P001/P002/P003/P004/P005/P006/P007/P010/P011/P014/P015/P016/P019/P020, and the predicate rules HC009/HC011. Vocabulary-binding pairs are read from one file through a classify()/link() call with a bind= keyword, so these rules fire from a single source too: HC004 (dead base type), HC005 (unused binding key), HC-P013 (routing key bound to a predicate). Link purity and emission: HC008, HC010. State reachability: HC-SM03. Feature flags, read from a module-scope FEATURES dict literal and feature_state() call sites: HC-HF001, HC-HF002. Suppression directives: HC-SUP001 (dead directive), HC-SUP002 (directive with no reason). Deferred to the probes, because a single source string cannot carry the context they read: HC001/HC002 (route-derived boundary vocabulary), HC-REF001-012 (route map, template roots, stylesheet classes, format manifest, cross-module .hd seams), HC-R001-R006/HC-OR001/HC-OR003/HC-A002 (the .hd role map, which the runner passes as None), HC-A001 (project-wide AuthProvider), HC-P018 (dynamic-dispatch call graph), HC-ST001/HC-ST002 (persist and DOM manifest). HC-SM04 (dead state) reads the state-machine's terminal set; HC-SM05-100 now declares its sink state terminal so an HC-SM04 case and HC-SM05-100 both pass. HC-P017 (serializer not declared as a chain link) reads the declared return-type annotation: a function annotated with an HTTP response type must be a @link with an emits vocabulary. HC-SM04 and HC-P017 are not yet wired into check_source, so their firing cases (HC-SM04-001, HC-P017-001) are expected-RED until the rules land.

cases.description: Source that does not parse fires HC-SYN and gates every other rule; the finding is file-level, so it carries no single line
A single if statement is a branch not expressed as a dispatch table
The if/elif/elif dispatch chain from spec section 9.2; one HC-P001 at the if line
The conditional expression a if cond else b is an if form and fires

input.source:
def f(x):
    return 1 if x else 0

cases.description: The if filter inside a comprehension is an if form and fires

input.source:
def f(xs):
    return [y for y in xs if y]

cases.description: The if __name__ == '__main__' script guard is exempt and fires nothing
A dict dispatch table read by a constant key is data, not a branch, and fires nothing
A match/case statement is not an if and fires nothing

input.source:
def f(x):
    match x:
        case 1:
            return 1
        case _:
            return 0

cases.description: A for loop is iteration, not a branch, and fires nothing
A bare class has an implicit object base, which is not approved
A class inheriting from a non-approved base fires
A TypedDict subclass is a data-shape declaration and fires nothing
A Protocol subclass is approved and fires nothing
A try/except inside a non-boundary function catches a fault in business logic
A try/finally with no except is cleanup, not a catch, and fires nothing
A non-boundary function that opens a file performs I/O in the interior
An isinstance check in business logic fires HC-P005
Plain arithmetic in business logic fires nothing
An lru_cache decorator with no profiling annotation fires HC-P006
Instance state assigned in a constructor fires HC-P007; the ABC base keeps HC-P003 silent
A call to a framework lifecycle hook fires HC-P011
Three functions with the same body once literals are blanked fire HC-P014 at the first
Two one-statement functions sharing a body stay below the two-function threshold and fire nothing
A parameter defaulting to a real value absorbs the caller's omission
Defaults of None, zero, and empty list are the honest encoding of absence and fire nothing

input.source:
def connect(timeout=None, retries=0, hosts=[]):
    return timeout

cases.description: An inner function that captures a name via nonlocal and mutates it fires HC-P016
An inner function that reads a nonlocal without mutating it fires nothing
A lookup with a fallback default serves an unknown key as a known one
A single-argument get reads without a fallback and fires nothing
A dispatch-table subscript with a variable key and no in-guard raises a bare KeyError on a miss
A dispatch-table subscript with a constant key is a fixed row, not a dispatch, and fires nothing
Two Set recognizers in one vocabulary sharing a value fire HC003 as an error
Two Set recognizers with disjoint values fire nothing
A composed type capturing a base type the vocabulary does not declare fires HC006
A composed type whose requires and captures both name declared base types fires nothing
A chain constructed with no links fires HC007
A predicate recognizer cannot be sampled statically, so honest-check emits an info directing the developer to the runtime check
A predicate that calls int() may throw on non-matching input; HC009 warns, and the same predicate draws the HC011 info
A transition naming a state outside the states vocabulary fires HC-SM01
A transition naming an event outside the events vocabulary fires HC-SM02
An initial state outside the states vocabulary fires HC-SM05
A state machine whose transition states, events, and initial state all sit in their vocabularies, and whose sink state 'paid' is declared terminal, fires nothing

input.source: m = state_machine(states=vocabulary({'s': {'pending', 'paid'}}), events=vocabulary({'e': {'pay'}}), initial='pending', transitions={('pending', 'pay'): 'paid'}, terminal={'paid'})

cases.description: A vocabulary base type that a paired binding neither binds nor composes is dead; the classify() call carries the vocabulary and its binding in the same file

input.source:
cards = vocabulary({'resource': {'users'}, 'ghost': {'phantom'}})
slots = binding({'resource': 'thing'})
classify('users', cards, bind=slots)

cases.description: A vocabulary whose every base type the paired binding binds fires nothing

input.source:
cards = vocabulary({'resource': {'users'}})
slots = binding({'resource': 'thing'})
classify('users', cards, bind=slots)

cases.description: A binding key that names no base type in the paired vocabulary is unused and fires HC005 at the binding

input.source:
cards = vocabulary({'resource': {'users'}})
slots = binding({'resource': 'thing', 'stray': 'slot'})
classify('users', cards, bind=slots)

cases.description: A link that is not a boundary and reads the clock in its body is impure; time.time() is nondeterministic, not I/O, so HC-P004 stays silent and only HC008 fires
A link declaring an emits type its body never produces fires HC010; the link returns its input manifest unchanged, so the emit type is phantom
A state in the states vocabulary that no transition reaches from the initial state is unreachable; 'extra' has an outgoing transition so it is not also dead, isolating HC-SM03
A two-state cycle reaches every state and leaves none without an outgoing transition, so neither HC-SM03 nor HC-SM04 fires
A pure function returning an instance of an in-file class fires HC-P010 at the return; the ABC base keeps HC-P003 silent and the instance is neither a TypedDict nor a read-only mapping
A routing-key slot (db_id) bound to a predicate recognizer lets an arbitrary identifier reach the pool; HC-P013 fires, and the same predicate draws the HC011 info

input.source:
v = vocabulary({'db': predicate(lambda s: True)})
b = binding({'db': 'db_id'})
classify('x', v, bind=b)

cases.description: The same routing-key slot bound to a bounded Set recognizer is a closed whitelist and fires nothing

input.source:
v = vocabulary({'db': {'main', 'replica'}})
b = binding({'db': 'db_id'})
classify('x', v, bind=b)

cases.description: A feature_state() call naming a flag absent from the module-scope FEATURES dict fires HC-HF001 at the call
A feature_state() call naming a flag declared in FEATURES fires nothing
A handler table dispatched by a flag state but missing an entry for one declared state ('off') fires HC-HF002
A handler table carrying an entry for every declared flag state fires nothing

input.source:
FEATURES = {'dark_mode': {'states': {'on', 'off'}}}
HANDLERS = {'on': on_handler, 'off': off_handler}; result = HANDLERS[feature_state('on', 'dark_mode')]

cases.description: An inline ignore of a rule that does not fire on its line is a dead directive; it carries a reason, so only HC-SUP001 fires

cases.description: An inline ignore whose rule fires on its line and that carries a reason suppresses that finding to info and draws neither suppression rule

input.source:

cases.description: An inline ignore that fires on its line but carries no reason suppresses the finding to info and fires HC-SUP002 for the missing reason

input.source:

cases.description: A reachable state 'paid' with no outgoing transition and not declared terminal is a dead state and fires HC-SM04; 'pending' has an outgoing transition and both states are reachable, so HC-SM03 stays silent and only HC-SM04 fires
The same sink state 'paid' declared terminal has no outgoing transition by design, so HC-SM04 stays silent

cases.description: A plain function whose return annotation is an HTTP response type produces HTTP output; without being a declared @link with an emits vocabulary it fires HC-P017 at its def line

The same HTTP-output function declared a @link with an emits vocabulary over the protocol surface satisfies the chain contract, so HC-P017 stays silent; accepts covers the emitted types so HC010 stays silent too
